result.title: Behavioral Affinity Transduction for Zero-Shot Vision-Language Classification
result.summary: An image that is hard to classify on its own may have a helpful neighbor in the same unlabeled batch. Zero-shot vision-language models (VLMs) score images independently and leave this evidence unused. We study small unlabeled query batches with no labeled examples. Visual similarity can reflect pose or background, so it may connect images from different classes. Each image's scores over the class vocabulary offer another way to choose neighbors. We introduce Behavioral Affinity Transduction (BAT), which builds a sparse graph from these class-response profiles. The graph supplies neighbor evidence during prediction. For EM-Dirichlet, it also screens candidate classes and initializes assignments. BAT plugs into direct and iterative readouts of a frozen VLM. Across diverse datasets, BAT improves the mean accuracy of every tested readout. In the main RN50 comparison, soft and hard EM-Dirichlet gain $4.22$ and $2.72$ percentage points.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Behavioral Affinity Transduction（BAT），在小规模无标签查询批次中，用冻结零样本 VLM 对类别词表的响应画像构建稀疏图，为直接式与迭代式读出提供近邻证据，并在 EM-Dirichlet 中用于类别筛选与初始化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用「类别响应画像」而非视觉相似度来挑选近邻证据，可供核查是否适用于 latent 推理中的视觉证据筛选与相似度度量设计；但论文聚焦零样本分类读出精度，未涉及推理状态生成或动态计算，联系有限。
